evals.name: work-auto-selects-one-item-via-seam-claim
evals.expected_output: Reclaims stale leases at session start (idempotent), auto-selects exactly ONE item from the frontier (open, unblocked, unassigned) via the seam list-frontier, then acquires it through the seam claim verb (assignee + lease record, race-safe) before executing it via the full 8-step workflow. The claim identity is the authenticated session user, never the bot.
expectations: Runs an idempotent session-start reclaim (`work-item-tracker.sh reclaim`) before selecting — never releases a live lease
Selects exactly ONE item to work — never claims multiple at once
Selects from the frontier via `work-item-tracker.sh list-frontier` (open, `blocked_by_count == 0`, unassigned); `--autonomous` additionally excludes `needs-human`
Acquires via the seam `work-item-tracker.sh claim` (assignee + lease comment, same-identity aware) — NOT a `status:considering`/`status:claimed` label hold protocol
On a lost race (`claim` exit 7) advances to the next candidate rather than retrying the same item

Executes the selected item through the 8-step workflow (/discovery:explore -> /discovery:research -> /planning:plan -> /implementation:implement -> /testing:plan -> /review:quality-gate -> /verification:confirm outcome -> /session-flow:retro)

evals.name: work-excludes-and-cross-references-remapped-recurring-role
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep. Both due maintenance and ordinary frontier items exist.
evals.expected_output: The work flow resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep before selection. It excludes scheduled-upkeep items from the non-recurring frontier tiers and uses scheduled-upkeep when listing open items for the recurring tiers. It never compares against or queries the default recurring literal.
expectations: Resolves the recurring-maintenance label before any tracker read
Excludes items carrying scheduled-upkeep from non-recurring frontier tiers
Uses --label scheduled-upkeep when cross-referencing recurring candidates
Does not fall back to the recurring literal after a valid remap
